notes: Notes: thin overcast upon arrival- skies cleared before leaving- temperatures climbed rapidly. Layer Notes: 69-66cm: friable -Feb 3; 30-27cm: aggregates remnant of crust. Stability tests column: CT24, SC @69cm; CT14, SC @69cm; ECTP23 @68cm; CT16, SC @31cm.
summary: Deep basal DH 0-60 cm (4-6 mm DH 0-27 cm with a 3 cm 'aggregates remnant of crust' layer at 27-30; rounding DH 2 mm 30-60.5 cm; hardness 1F at the base fading to 4F then back to 1F) under a thin ice-hard (I) layer at 60.5-61 cm, FC 61-66 (1F), friable MFcl layer 66-69 cm (P, 'Feb 3'), FCxr 69-105 cm (1F- then 1F+ to P gradient), DF 105-113 and moist MF 113-115; CT24 and CT14 SC at 69 cm, ECTP23 at 68 cm, CT16 SC at 31 cm; HS 115 cm; surface 0 C (air +2 C)
reading_issues: Hardness bars, boundaries and temperature dots were measured from pixels. Three layers are trapezoids (hardness gradients) and hardness_idx is the mean of the top and bottom values: 0-27 cm 1F(base)->4F(top); 30-60.5 cm 4F(base)->1F(top); 75-105 cm P(base)->1F+(top). The 60.5-61 cm thin layer has a blank form and size and I-hardness; class IF is inferred from the hardness. Glyphs: the flat-topped 'Λ with crossbar' at 27-60.5 cm is read as rounding depth hoar (DHxr, flagged uncertain); the 0-27 cm glyph (Λ with an extra stroke) is read as DH. Temperature profile only covers 60-115 cm. Tests at 69 cm sit at the top of the 66-69 cm MFcl layer; ECTP23 at 68 cm is inside it (layer_grain MF). Top 'surface form' row blank, so surface_grain is null.
